title: Crewbrain — demo
ttsInstructions: Speak like a calm, confident product founder walking a colleague through a live demo. Plain and warm, measured pace, no hype. Leave a short natural pause between sentences.

segments.name: problem
segments.headline: Every answer lives in the owner's head
segments.caption: Homeowners, crews and the office all call one person.
segments.narration: Meet Sam. He runs Rivera Solar and Electric, a small crew doing panels, batteries and service upgrades. Every day his phone rings with the same questions. A homeowner wants to know what her panel warranty covers. A roofing crew needs the gate code for the job. The apprentice asks which breaker feeds the inverter. The answers exist, but they live in Sam's head, his inbox and his Drive. And sharing a folder means sharing everything in it, including the price book.

segments.name: market
segments.headline: Small trade contractors
segments.caption: About 600,000 US specialty trade contractors with payroll.
segments.narration: Crewbrain is built for small trade contractors like Sam. Electricians, solar installers, roofers, HVAC and plumbing shops. There are about six hundred thousand specialty trade contractor businesses with payroll in the United States. Seventy-nine percent of small business owners say they know about AI agents, but only sixteen percent have actually deployed one. We think the gap is trust. Who gets to see what, and for how long.

segments.name: brain
segments.headline: Snap it. Approve it. Lock it.
segments.caption: Every item in the company brain carries a lock.
segments.narration: First, Sam builds his company brain. He snaps a photo of the warranty card from a SunPeak panel. Claude reads the card and drafts a knowledge item, with the coverage terms and the serial number. But nothing is usable until Sam approves it. He checks the draft, picks who can see it, and taps approve. It lands in the brain with a lock on it. Every item has one: office only, crew for the Oak Street job, or homeowners. Documents that come in from Google Drive arrive with their sharing already attached, so Sam doesn't start from zero.

segments.name: create
segments.headline: Say what you need. Approve the card.
segments.caption: The creator agent drafts a helper. Sam approves it.
segments.narration: Now Sam talks to the creator agent, by voice or by text. He asks for a helper for the Patels about their install at forty-two Oak Street, to stay around until thirty days after handover. The creator asks only for what's missing. Then it shows an approval card. Who the helper is for. What it knows. What it can check, and what it can do. What it can't see. And exactly when it ends. Sam taps approve, and Juno is live, with a QR code and a personal link to share with the Patels. Then he does the same for Bay Roofing's crew. Rex is ready, and he ends when the job closes on Friday at six.

segments.name: use
segments.headline: Answers with sources. Actions, not just chat.
segments.caption: Juno answers the Patels. Rex briefs the crew, in Spanish.
segments.narration: Here is the homeowner's side. Mrs. Patel opens Juno from her link and asks what her warranty covers. Juno answers from the approved warranty card, and shows exactly which source it used. When she wants to see the system in person, Juno can request a walkthrough, and that lands in Sam's inbox. On the roof, a Bay Roofing crew member asks Rex for the gate code, in Spanish, by voice. Rex answers in Spanish. Then he snaps a photo of a cracked flashing, and Rex logs it as an issue for Sam, with the photo attached. Helpers don't just answer questions. They take small actions Sam approved.

segments.name: locks
segments.headline: They see only what they're allowed. Then they end.
segments.caption: Search runs as the audience. Access changes apply instantly.
segments.narration: Now let's prove the locks. Juno is asked for the gate code, and she refuses, because that item is locked to the crew, not homeowners. Ask any helper for the price book, and it never comes back, because it's office only. A different company running on the same server sees nothing of Rivera's at all. Then Sam taps close job. Rex's open chat on the crew member's phone ends on the spot, and the crew brief relocks to office only. Nobody has to remember to revoke anything. And every one of these checks runs as an automated access test, on every change.

segments.name: how
segments.headline: Policy first, then the brain
segments.caption: Phone · server policy · HydraDB · Claude · gpt-realtime
segments.narration: Here's how it works. Every request from the phone passes server policy checks first: who is asking, which helper, and is it still active. HydraDB holds the company brain, with a separate database per company and an access list on every source. Search runs as the audience, so a helper can't retrieve what its audience can't see, and access changes apply instantly. Claude does the reasoning and the actions, and OpenAI's realtime voice lets everyone just talk.

segments.name: close
segments.headline: Your company brain, with locks on it
segments.caption: Try it: macmini.tail435588.ts.net:10000/crewbrain
segments.narration: That's Crewbrain. A company brain with locks on it, and helpers that know only what they should, and end when the job ends. Try it at the link on screen, and the code is on GitHub.
